solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pleasure associated with good American smut perhaps

parts.note: pleasure or enjoyment is fun
US, short for United States, stands for American

explanation.surface: A prude complains about enjoyment linked to good old American filth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smut' looks like dirty talk, but it is the plant disease, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is a parasitic growth on cereal crops, an example of this kind of organism.

clue.text: Odd parts of tunnel removed, so one breaks free

indicators.note: odd parts of the word tunnel are its first, third and fifth letters
removed says those odd letters go, leaving the even ones
breaks says the letters of so one are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: Half a tunnel is dug away so a prisoner escapes.
explanation.definitionFit: To loosen or release something is to set it free; a verb synonym.

clue.text: After a couple of drinks, fancy a game?

indicators.note: after places the next piece behind the drinks

parts.note: gin and rum are two drinks
gin and rum are two drinks
my! is an exclamation of surprise, like fancy!

explanation.surface: An invitation to play cards after a couple of rounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' looks like 'would you like', but it is the exclamation 'fancy that!'
explanation.definitionFit: This is a card game for two or more players, melding sets and runs.

clue.text: Winter weather to deal with in a wild part of Wales

parts.note: snow is typical winter weather
to do a task is to deal with it

indicators.note: wild means the letters of in a run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Snowy conditions to cope with in rugged Welsh country.
explanation.definitionFit: This mountainous national park in north-west Wales is a region of that country.

clue.text: Influence assumed by a clergyman

indicators.note: to be assumed by is to be taken on or taken in by, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
reach is range of influence or power

explanation.surface: A vicar takes on the role of moral authority in the parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' does double duty in the surface reading but in the wordplay it is the Latin-derived word meaning by, which takes in the influence.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is someone whose job includes delivering sermons, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Summer speciality? A pathetic summer trip?

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters of a pathetic summer fall over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone's dismal holiday is their seasonal highlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Summer' twice reads as the season, but in the definition it is one who sums, a person who adds up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does sums might specialise in abstract numerical theory, the field of numbers studied for itself.

clue.text: Sensitivity and resistance finally easing in back passage

indicators.note: in says the two pieces go inside the word for back passage

parts.note: an alley is a narrow passage behind buildings
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of easing

explanation.surface: A medical-sounding note about gentle relief in an intimate area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back passage' reads as anatomy but is a lane behind houses.
explanation.definitionFit: An abnormal reaction of the body to a substance is a heightened sensitivity to it.

clue.text: Attention seeker grabs something prized — active control

indicators.note: grabs means the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: hey! is a call seeking attention
a gem is a prized thing
on means working or active

explanation.surface: A show-off snatches a treasure and takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Dominance of one state or group over others is political control.

clue.text: After bible class, urgent scramble to stand up

indicators.note: after puts the following piece behind the class

parts.note: RI, religious instruction, was the school bible class

indicators.note: scramble means the letters of urgent are mixed up

explanation.surface: After Sunday school, a hurried rush to get to one's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand up' looks physical but means hold good, as a story does under scrutiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim that stands up seems convincing and credible; an idiom for sounding genuine.

clue.text: Group shot — as individual characters you are forming a row

parts.note: a clan is a group of families
a shot is a go, an attempt
'you are' written as single letters, as in texting, is U R

explanation.surface: A team photo where every member spells out a letter, standing in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a line of people, as the surface suggests, but it is a noisy din.
explanation.definitionFit: A row in the sense of a loud racket or din is a harsh clashing noise.

clue.text: Label applied to bottle

parts.note: to flag something is to label or mark it
something applied to a surface is on it

explanation.surface: Instructions to stick a label on a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A large vessel with a handle and spout for holding wine or cider is a kind of bottle.

clue.text: Mineral company managed to have ditch shortened

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it

indicators.note: shortened means the word for ditch loses its last letter

parts.note: to ditch something is to dump it

explanation.surface: A mining firm was allowed to dig a shorter trench.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard crystalline form of aluminium oxide, which includes ruby and sapphire, is a mineral.

clue.text: Ballpoint ready?

parts.note: split in two, ball gives PROM, a dance
the second half, point, gives PT, its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pen is set to write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ballpoint' reads as one word for a pen, but split it into ball, a dance, and point.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quick to act, or on time, is being ready; a synonym in the sense of alert.

clue.text: Artist wants a line of LSD?

parts.note: Claude Monet was a French Impressionist painter
RY, short for railway, is a line

explanation.surface: A painter is after a hit of the hallucinogenic drug.
explanation.walkthrough: LSD is not the drug but pounds, shillings and pence (Latin librae, solidi, denarii), Britain's pre-1971 money.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything to do with pounds, shillings and pence relates to money, so it is financial.

clue.text: Downpour imminent but no closer? Put stuff outside

indicators.note: outside says the word for stuff goes around the other piece

parts.note: to ram is to stuff or cram

indicators.note: no closer means the phrase for imminent loses its last letter

parts.note: something in store is about to happen, imminent

explanation.surface: Rain is coming but no nearer, so put things out.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy fall of rain with wind is a downpour.

clue.text: Very dark part of 16…

parts.note: something that is part of a whole is in it
16 down is the American state, whose postal abbreviation is KY

explanation.surface: A shadowy region of the state named in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to the next, but the wordplay here stands alone: to be part of Kentucky is to be in KY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something black as ink is very dark.

clue.text: Independent carelessly printed in bold

indicators.note: carelessly suggests the letters of printed set down out of order

explanation.surface: The Independent newspaper sloppily put something in heavy type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bold' looks like typeface, but means fearless.
explanation.definitionFit: Fearless and daring people are bold.

clue.text: New food in central Derby location

indicators.note: in places the new food inside the word for central

parts.note: key means central or crucial
tuck is British schoolchild slang for food, especially sweets

explanation.surface: Fresh food arrives at a venue in the middle of Derby, an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derby' looks like the English city, but it is the Kentucky Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous American horse race is run at Churchill Downs in Louisville, so the state is its location.

clue.text: …in very desirable part of IOW

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words very desirable

explanation.surface: A sought-after district of the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: IOW is the Isle of Wight, an island off England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is a ferry port on the island's north-east coast, so a place in it.

clue.text: Warbler crossword ultimately fills leisure time with cunning

indicators.note: fills means a letter goes inside the word for leisure time

parts.note: rest is time off, leisure

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of crossword

parts.note: art can mean craft or cunning

explanation.surface: A puzzle fills a crafty person's spare hours.
explanation.definitionFit: This small songbird with a red tail is called a warbler loosely, as a singing bird.

clue.text: I don't think about what could kill bully

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the second

parts.note: a doer is an active type, not a thinker, so 'I don't think' could be a doer speaking
a mine is an explosive that could kill

explanation.surface: A sceptic contemplates a lethal weapon to deal with a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I don't think' sounds like scepticism but is a self-description by someone who acts rather than thinks.
explanation.definitionFit: To bully is to order others about arrogantly.

clue.text: Ointment container's shape

parts.note: a vase is a container for flowers
a line is an outline or shape

explanation.surface: Describing the form of a jar of cream.
explanation.definitionFit: This petroleum jelly is a soothing ointment, the brand name now generic.

clue.text: Plastic bags beginning to rustle under church organs

indicators.note: bags means grabs or holds, so the card name surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Visa is a credit card, slangily plastic

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts this letter below the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: beginning to takes the first letter of rustle

explanation.surface: Plastic bags rustle beneath a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organs' looks musical, but it means the body's internal parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The innards of the body are its internal organs.

clue.text: Setter failed another examination

indicators.note: failed suggests the letters of setter break down and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: The puzzle compiler flunked and must sit a resit.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine something again is to run a fresh test of it; here the noun for a second check.

clue.text: Offer a ship as second home

parts.note: SS, short for steamship, is a ship
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A sales pitch: buy a vessel to use as a holiday home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offer' looks like a proposal, but read it as off-er: one who offs, slang for kills.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'off' means kill, so an off-er is a killer, especially a hired one.

clue.text: Announcement of legal contract

indicators.note: an announcement is spoken aloud, so the word for legal is heard rather than written

parts.note: pukka, from Hindi, means genuine or legitimate

explanation.surface: A formal statement of a binding legal agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a legal noun but is the verb, to draw together.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrinkle or gather into folds, as lips do, is to contract.

clue.text: One special load set apart

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: special hints at letters made into something out of the ordinary, a rearrangement of load and set

explanation.surface: A single exceptional cargo is kept separate from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'special' looks like S and 'set apart' like the definition; instead LOADSET is rearranged to OLADSET... giving SOLATED after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cut off and alone stands apart from everything else.

clue.text: Stone barriers, oddly dirty, used to be split by lines

indicators.note: oddly means take the odd-numbered letters of dirty
split by says one word is broken open and the other put in the gap

parts.note: was is the past tense of be
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: Grubby walls were divided up by lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Walls built of stone without mortar are field barriers common in upland Britain.

clue.text: Old Vic?

definitions.meaning: old in the sense of grown up, fully developed
The question mark flags a name used as an example

explanation.surface: The Old Vic is a famous London theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripe and grown up means old; Vic is Victor, the 1950s film star of that surname.
